tool.name: SBDI taxonomic annotation
tool.description: format taxonomy and optional screening predictions for reannotation
tool.command: sed '1s/^[^\t]*/ASV_ID/' '$taxonomy' > taxonomy.tsv && #if $predictions sed '1s/^[^\t]*/ASV_ID/' '$predictions' > predictions.tsv && #end if Rscript '$__tool_directory__/sbdiexportreannotate.R' '$reference_database' taxonomy.tsv '$taxonomy_method' '$analysis_version' '$its_region' #if $predictions predictions.tsv #end if

param.name: taxonomy
param.label: ASV taxonomy table
param.help: First column: ASV identifier. Required named columns include sequence and confidence; optional ranks and SH/BOLD identifiers are retained.

param.name: predictions
param.label: Sequence screening predictions
param.help: First column: matching ASV identifier. Remaining columns are joined to the annotation table.

param.name: reference_database
param.label: Reference database provenance
param.help: Name, version and optional persistent URL of the database actually used for classification.

param.name: analysis_version
param.label: Upstream analysis provenance label
param.help: The source formatter includes this label in annotation_algorithm after Ampliseq. Set it to describe the analysis that actually produced the input taxonomy.

tool.help:
Format existing taxonomy and optional sequence-screening predictions as an SBDI reannotation table. Scientific names, rank, species hypotheses, confidence, sequences and supplied screening fields are retained. This tool does not perform classification.
The first identifier header is normalized to `ASV_ID`. Taxonomy requires `sequence` and `confidence`; absent optional ranks are left empty. The prediction table is joined by ASV identifier, never row position.
`date_identified` records the export execution date. `reference_db` and `annotation_algorithm` describe user-supplied upstream provenance. The inherited formatter prefixes the algorithm label with Ampliseq; use the analysis provenance parameter to distinguish a native Galaxy analysis from an nf-core execution. Dates, paths and provenance labels are not scientific agreement criteria.
The format-normalized MIT-licensed formatter is from nf-core/ampliseq 2.11.0, commit 0473e157ac9a7b1d36845ff9f8fa7ac843d3b234; original author Daniel Lundin.
